submitter: bugs_open/204 lane, commit C (the write-side guard)
rationale:
SEPARATE from this lane's A/B submission (corr f73f4eeb) on purpose, and the separation is the first thing to review. A/B fixed the PRODUCER: validate_plan no longer deletes a section name that is a positional slot the page already carries. This is the CONSUMER, and it is a class defence — it refuses an empty sections list over a real one whatever produced it, including causes nobody has found yet. Different mechanism, different blast radius (upsertPage has one Go caller but three live agents reach it: build-site-planner's sync_pages, pageflow-builder and site-work-orchestrator), and the A/B fix is complete without it.

THE DEFECT. site_db_actions.go:1201 carries `sections = EXCLUDED.sections`, unconditional. Its two immediate neighbours IN THE SAME ON CONFLICT STATEMENT were given destructive-write guards on 2026-08-19 after blank overwrites were measured on robot-hands.com: nav_label = COALESCE(NULLIF(pages.nav_label,''), EXCLUDED...), meta_description = COALESCE(NULLIF(EXCLUDED...,''), pages.meta_description). The jsonb column between them was left unguarded, and it is the one whose loss is unrecoverable.

WHY SECTIONS IS THE WORST OF THE THREE. pages.sections is the ONLY record of a decomposed page's composition. page_components keeps serving after it is emptied, so the site looks fine and nothing alerts; the damage surfaces only when the next rebuild finds nothing to rebuild and builds an empty page over a live one. Measured 2026-08-20: one replan emptied 41 of 45 live pages on loanandmortgagecalculator.co.uk and queued 20 needs_page items against them, all claimable within seconds. Contained and reversed from a pre-fire snapshot within the hour — but the containment was a human noticing, not a control.

THE SHAPE, and how it reconciles with plan-authority. LANDMINES records that this helper deliberately carries `page_type = EXCLUDED.page_type` because 'it is the plan-sync path, where the plan is the authority on what a page is'. That stays true here: the plan remains authoritative for every NON-EMPTY proposal, so a recomposition still wins — exactly as meta_description's guard lets a real incoming value win and refuses only a blank. Only the non-empty -> empty transition is intercepted. Sections differs from page_type in the way the incident proved: a wrong page_type is visible and rewritable by the next plan; an emptied section list destroys the only record there is.

ZERO SECTIONS STAYS REPRESENTABLE, and this is measured rather than assumed: 72 of 748 active pages live legitimately at sections=[] , 60 of them tools [MEASURED 2026-08-21]. Three doors stay open — empty-over-empty is untouched, every INSERT is untouched (the guard is in the ON CONFLICT branch only), and a deliberate emptying travels through the recompose_pages release. That release is the EXISTING channel that already means 'this page is released for redesign' (recomposePagesFromSpec, read by validate_plan today), so this adds no config key and asks no operator to remember anything new — and a reviewer of the CALLER can see the intent, which is what the 2026-08-02 §2 ruling is actually about.

A REFUSAL IS DURABLE, NOT LOGGED. A silent keep would mean the write reports success while the plan and the database quietly disagree about what a page is made of — which is bugs_open/204 in a new place, and on a service whose logs rotate sub-second a Warn is not a record. PAGE_SECTIONS_EMPTY_OVERWRITE_REFUSED names the pages and points at the upstream cause, and its remedy text states the thing a reader most needs: the DATABASE is what the site is built from, not the plan they are reading.

TWO OF FIVE MUTATIONS SURVIVED THE FIRST PASS, and I would rather the council heard it from me. (1) Mutating the RETURNING expression to `false AND ...` changed nothing, because sqlmock never executes SQL — the test proved only that the Go SCANS the column. Closed by pinning the expression as TEXT, with the test stating plainly what that can and cannot establish (that the statement asks the right question; NOT that Postgres answers it correctly — the verification plan induces a live row for that). (2) Replacing the per-page lookup at the call site with a constant made the release SITE-WIDE and left every test green, because they all stopped at upsertPage's boundary — one legitimately-recomposed page would have licensed emptying every other page in the run. Closed by an integration test driving the whole action with two pages, one released and one not. The generalisable finding is in the register entry: a guard tested only at the helper's boundary is untested against the wiring that decides its input.

KNOWN EDGE, stated rather than left to be discovered: recompose_pages names realised page names while the sync loop reads the CANONICALISED name, so a page whose canonical name differs may not match the release. The failure direction is the safe one — the emptying is refused and durably recorded, naming the page and the remedy — but it is real.

NOT GUARDED, deliberately and enumerated: apply_gap_plan's retype UPDATE and its applyNewPage conflict arm (both incoming lists are non-empty by construction, so this shape would be inert on them), and adopt_verbatim / apply_adoption_plan / create_blog_posts / UpsertPageForRole (different authorities, none downstream of the resolver). Named so nobody reads this as fleet-wide cover for sections writes. It is not.

plan.summary: One commit. upsertPage's `sections = EXCLUDED.sections` becomes a four-arm CASE parameterised by an explicit release flag, single-statement and race-free; RETURNING gains a sections_kept column so a refusal reaches the caller rather than being silent; SyncPagesToDBAction threads the EXISTING recompose_pages release per page and files one durable finding naming the refused pages. Plan-authority is unchanged for every non-empty proposal. 7 tests, 5 mutations run and 5 killed — two only after the tests were strengthened, both recorded.

edits.symbol: upsertPage (the ON CONFLICT sections clause + RETURNING) and SyncPagesToDBAction (the release + the durable record)
edits.rationale: The guard is a CASE rather than a COALESCE because the condition is emptiness of a jsonb array, not NULL-ness, and because the release flag has to be the first arm — a caller that has declared the emptying deliberate must not then be second-guessed by the emptiness test. Single statement, so there is no read-then-write window for a concurrent sync to slip through. RETURNING is widened rather than a second SELECT for the same reason. The release is read per page from the set recomposePagesFromSpec already builds, so validate_plan and sync_pages_to_db cannot disagree about which pages are released — they read one function.
edits.sketch:
sections = CASE
	WHEN $13::bool THEN EXCLUDED.sections                                        -- deliberate, declared by the caller
	WHEN COALESCE(jsonb_array_length(EXCLUDED.sections), 0) > 0 THEN EXCLUDED.sections  -- plan still authoritative
	WHEN COALESCE(jsonb_array_length(pages.sections), 0) = 0 THEN EXCLUDED.sections     -- nothing to protect
	ELSE pages.sections                                                          -- the refusal
END,
...
RETURNING ..., (COALESCE(jsonb_array_length(sections), 0) > 0
                AND COALESCE(jsonb_array_length($11::jsonb), 0) = 0) AS sections_kept

edits.symbol: 7 tests over all four directions plus the wiring
edits.rationale: All four directions, because a guard that only ever keeps is as broken as one that only ever overwrites: empty-over-non-empty KEEPS; the same WITH the release overwrites; non-empty-over-non-empty overwrites (this is what stops the guard freezing the column, the failure the sibling meta_description test warns about one file over); empty-over-empty writes with no noise. Two tests exist only because mutations survived: the RETURNING expression is pinned as text (sqlmock does not execute SQL, so the behavioural-looking test was textual and said so), and an integration test drives the whole action with two pages to prove the release is decided PER PAGE at the statement rather than site-wide.

edits.symbol: the two upsertPage call sites and their RETURNING mocks
edits.rationale: Mechanical: upsertPage gained a parameter and a returned column, so the 2026-08-19 sibling guard's tests need both. Worth naming in this submission rather than passing over as noise, because those tests are the precedent this change is modelled on and a reviewer should see they still pass unchanged in substance — the guard they pin is untouched.

Ordering-exemption condition 2 — a shared seam is registered in the same commit that ships it. The entry states what another workstream needs: recompose_pages now governs more than the planner's convergence, so a flow that legitimately empties a page must name it there. It also carries both surviving-mutation findings and the canonical-name edge, because those are what a later reader would otherwise have to rediscover.

### PLAN-052 — `pages.sections` is non-destructible by a sync

grounded_in: site_db_actions.go:1201 before this change: `sections = EXCLUDED.sections,` with no guard, between `nav_label = COALESCE(NULLIF(pages.nav_label, ''), EXCLUDED.nav_label),` and `meta_description = COALESCE(NULLIF(EXCLUDED.meta_description, ''), pages.meta_description),` — both added 2026-08-19 after measured blank overwrites on robot-hands.com (four pages holding 97/120/169/329 chars in an April snapshot reading 0).

bugs_open/204 CONTRIBUTION 2026-08-20: 41 of 45 live pages emptied on loanandmortgagecalculator.co.uk in one replan; 20 needs_page + 1 needs_rerender + 1 needs_design + 5 needs_imagery filed and cancelled; sections restored from a pre-fire snapshot. 'sync_pages' upsert does `sections = EXCLUDED.sections` unconditionally (no COALESCE, unlike its nav_label/meta_description neighbours), so [] overwrote three real slot names on each affected page.

Zero-sections population [MEASURED 2026-08-21]: SELECT count(*) FROM pages WHERE status='active' -> 748; of those, 72 have jsonb_array_length(COALESCE(sections,'[]'))=0, and 60 of those 72 are page_type='tool'. So the empty state is legitimate and common, and making it unreachable would be a worse defect than the one being fixed.

upsertPage's reach [MEASURED 2026-08-21]: exactly one Go caller (SyncPagesToDBAction, site_db_actions.go:364), but the action is wired into three live agents — build-site-planner (step `sync_pages`), pageflow-builder and site-work-orchestrator (step `sync_pages_to_db`).

recomposePagesFromSpec (v3_site_actions.go:7630) reads input_data.spec.recompose_pages and is already the explicit-redesign channel read by validate_plan — so the release reused here is an existing mechanism with an existing meaning, not a new flag.

LANDMINES 'There are THREE `pages` upsert helpers and they have OPPOSITE collision policies': site_db_actions.upsertPage 'carries page_type = EXCLUDED.page_type and will re-type whatever it collides with (correct for it — it is the plan-sync path, where the plan is the authority on what a page is)'. page_type stays unguarded here for exactly that reason.

Mutation results: 5 run, 5 killed — but two only after the tests were strengthened. RETURNING expression -> `false AND ...` initially left the suite GREEN (sqlmock does not execute SQL); per-page release -> site-wide constant initially left the suite GREEN (every test stopped at upsertPage's boundary). Both gaps closed and both recorded in the register entry.
Full platform/orchestration/actions and platform/orchestration/datahelpers suites green after the change.
